text:
Recent work supports testing stronger negative objectives, but does not establish that single-negative training specifically explains Electronics performance. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024 extended abstract)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) identifies overconfidence and training instability from sampled BCE; its generalized BCE corrects this while retaining sampling. [eSASRec (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) finds SASRec’s sequential objective combined with LiGR layers and sampled softmax competitive, without extra features. These motivate separate multi-negative sampled-softmax and gBCE ablations; eSASRec’s combined results do not isolate the loss contribution.

Hardness needs scheduling and false-negative controls. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) reports problems with introducing hard negatives early and fixed hardest-item selection; it combines uniform warm-start, efficient global candidate recall, and curriculum re-ranking. [CATS (SIGIR 2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) adaptively samples across item clusters, reducing same-positive-cluster sampling over time to mitigate suspected false negatives. Cluster similarity is a heuristic, not proof that an unobserved item is positive.

Practical inference for RecHarness: first isolate negative count and loss, then test a warm-started mixture of uniform and moderately hard negatives. Exclude padding, target IDs, and observed training positives; use training-derived embeddings for optional similarity filtering. Compare against uniform sampling because a [2024 sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity tradeoffs. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10 across all four categories; inspect Electronics separately, but treat improved training margins as diagnostics rather than evidence of ranking gains.
